cases.question: On 29 July 2026, Sydney time, at which five-minute interval was NSW dispatch total demand highest across the whole day, and what was the level?

gold_numbers.label: NSW1 maximum dispatch total demand over 29 Jul AEST (interval ending 19:05 AEST)

expected.check: A correct answer gives the maximum over all 288 intervals of 29 July AEST (window (14:00Z 28 Jul, 14:00Z 29 Jul]) with its interval (ending 09:05Z = 19:05 AEST) and level; it must not report operational demand or a maximum over another window.

provenance.gold_method: Window = local day 29 Jul AEST = (2026-07-28T14:00Z, 2026-07-29T14:00Z], 288 intervals confirmed. Max of totaldemand_mw; tie check by equality with the max (one row); next-highest = second row by value.
queries: SELECT count(*) AS n FROM regionsum_5min WHERE region='NSW1' AND interval_end_utc > TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-07-28 14:00:00+00' AND interval_end_utc <= TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-07-29 14:00:00+00'

SELECT row_id, interval_end_utc, totaldemand_mw FROM regionsum_5min WHERE region='NSW1' AND interval_end_utc > TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-07-28 14:00:00+00' AND interval_end_utc <= TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-07-29 14:00:00+00' ORDER BY totaldemand_mw DESC, interval_end_utc LIMIT 3

SELECT row_id, interval_end_utc, totaldemand_mw FROM regionsum_5min WHERE region='NSW1' AND interval_end_utc > TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-07-28 14:00:00+00' AND interval_end_utc <= TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-07-29 14:00:00+00' AND totaldemand_mw = (SELECT max(totaldemand_mw) FROM regionsum_5min WHERE region='NSW1' AND interval_end_utc > TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-07-28 14:00:00+00' AND interval_end_utc <= TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-07-29 14:00:00+00')

cases.question: Which half-hour on 29 July 2026 (Brisbane time) had Queensland's highest operational demand, and how many MW was it?

gold_numbers.label: QLD1 maximum operational demand over 29 Jul AEST (half-hour 18:00-18:30 AEST), latest revision

expected.check: A correct answer gives the half-hour ending 08:30Z (18:00-18:30 AEST) and its operational demand from the latest revision; it must not give the runner-up half-hour ending 09:00Z (1 MW lower) or a dispatch total demand figure.

provenance.gold_method: Window = 48 half-hours of 29 Jul AEST, (2026-07-28T14:00Z, 2026-07-29T14:00Z]. Latest revision per half-hour = greatest available_at_utc ('updated' daily row). Max, tie check by equality, next-highest = second row.
queries: SELECT count(DISTINCT interval_end_utc) AS n FROM opdemand_actual WHERE region='QLD1' AND interval_end_utc > TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-07-28 14:00:00+00' AND interval_end_utc <= TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-07-29 14:00:00+00'

WITH latest AS (SELECT * FROM opdemand_actual WHERE region='QLD1' AND interval_end_utc > TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-07-28 14:00:00+00' AND interval_end_utc <= TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-07-29 14:00:00+00' QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY interval_end_utc ORDER BY available_at_utc DESC) = 1) SELECT row_id, interval_end_utc, revision, operational_demand_mw FROM latest ORDER BY operational_demand_mw DESC, interval_end_utc LIMIT 3

WITH latest AS (SELECT * FROM opdemand_actual WHERE region='QLD1' AND interval_end_utc > TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-07-28 14:00:00+00' AND interval_end_utc <= TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-07-29 14:00:00+00' QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY interval_end_utc ORDER BY available_at_utc DESC) = 1) SELECT row_id FROM latest WHERE operational_demand_mw = (SELECT max(operational_demand_mw) FROM latest)

highest TAS1 TOTALDEMAND on the local day, interval ending 2026-07-28T21:55Z (07:55 Hobart)

SELECT row_id, interval_end_utc, rrp FROM price_5min WHERE region='TAS1' AND interval_end_utc > '2026-07-28T14:00:00Z' AND interval_end_utc <= '2026-07-29T14:00:00Z' ORDER BY rrp DESC LIMIT 1

SELECT row_id, interval_end_utc, totaldemand_mw FROM regionsum_5min WHERE region='TAS1' AND interval_end_utc > '2026-07-28T14:00:00Z' AND interval_end_utc <= '2026-07-29T14:00:00Z' ORDER BY totaldemand_mw DESC LIMIT 1

cases.question: What was the highest dispatch total demand (TOTALDEMAND) in Queensland across the whole of Wednesday 29 July 2026, Brisbane local time, and when did that peak happen?
cases.writer_notes: QLD1 chosen: the brief excludes NSW1 and TAS1, and VIC1's 29 July 2026 day is development material (any measure). QLD1's development item for that day is operational demand only, so dispatch total demand on QLD1 is not development material. Window is fully held for total demand (288 of 288 five-minute intervals). QLD1 has no daylight saving, so the day is 24 hours at +10:00.

cases.question: For SA1, over the full local day of 29 July 2026 (midnight to midnight, Adelaide time), which 5-minute interval carried the day's top dispatch total demand, and what level did it hit?
cases.writer_notes: SA1 chosen: with F01 = QLD1 and NSW1/TAS1 excluded, the only other candidate is VIC1, whose 29 July 2026 day is development material. The SA1 day itself is not development material, but it contains one development half-hour (SA1, ending 2026-07-29T08:00:00Z); this cannot be avoided because every remaining region's day is development material. Fully held: 288 of 288 intervals. Tests the +09:30 offset.

cases.question: Across New South Wales' whole local day, Wednesday 29 July 2026 by Sydney clocks from midnight to midnight, which half-hour saw the maximum operational demand, and what was the level?
cases.writer_notes: NSW1 chosen: QLD1 is excluded by the brief, and TAS1/VIC1 29 July 2026 days are development material for any measure. NSW1's development item for that day is total demand only, so operational demand there is not listed. The day contains one development half-hour (NSW1, ending 2026-07-28T21:30:00Z); SA1, the only alternative, also contains one, so this cannot be avoided; NSW1 was preferred to spread regions (SA1 is already F02). Fully held: 48 of 48 half-hours.

cases.question: On Hobart clocks, covering the whole of Sunday 5 April 2026, how high did TAS1 operational demand peak and in which half-hour?
cases.writer_notes: TAS1 chosen to spread regions; it observes daylight saving, which ended on 5 April 2026, so the local day is 25 hours (50 half-hours, all held). No development material covers April 2026. The question deliberately does not mention the 25-hour length, so the assistant must work it out.

cases.question: Within the request's window for NSW1 (2 pm to 9 pm AEDT, Sydney daylight time, on Saturday 4 April 2026), find the maximum operational demand and report the half-hour it was recorded in.
cases.writer_notes: Explicit 7-hour window on half-hour boundaries, inside the NSW1 operational-demand held range 2026-04-03T18:00Z to 2026-04-05T18:00Z (14 of 14 half-hours held). Not a whole local day or an event window. Words match the fields: 2 pm and 9 pm AEDT (+11:00, daylight saving still in force on 4 April) are 03:00Z and 10:00Z. Operational demand is used here so that F06 can use total demand. No development material covers April 2026.

cases.question: Thinking about the Victorian high-price event of 20 August 2026, how high did VIC1 dispatch total demand (TOTALDEMAND) go over that event's full window, and when was the top reached?
cases.writer_notes: Event VIC1-20260820T0910-hi: the only VIC1 event on 20 August 2026 and the only high-price event that day, so region + kind + date identify it uniquely. Not development material (unlike VIC1-20260728T2120-lo, SA1-20260731T0235-hi and the TAS1 6 August day; NSW1-20260731T0730-hi and SA1-20260729T1755-hi contain development half-hours). Fully held for total demand: 294 of 294 intervals. Identified by date rather than peak time so the question carries no time that might coincide with the answer.

cases.question: Based only on data published by noon Brisbane time on Sunday 5 October 2025, what was the highest operational demand in Queensland over that entire local day, and at what time?
cases.writer_notes: QLD1 local day 5 October 2025 (fully held, 48 half-hours; not development material; 24 hours since QLD1 has no daylight saving). Cutoff 2025-10-05T02:00:00Z = noon AEST, strictly inside the window. By the cutoff 8 half-hours have a public row (published 2025-10-04T21:26Z) and 40 do not (earliest publication 2025-10-05T21:26Z), so the whole-day maximum cannot be established as of the cutoff. The question asks for the whole day's maximum and names the cutoff in words that match the field.

cases.question: During Tasmania's 31 July 2026 high-price episode, how far did demand climb and when did it top out?
cases.writer_notes: Names no measure (only 'demand'), so a careful assistant must ask whether dispatch total demand or operational demand is meant. Otherwise in scope: TAS1, and the window of event TAS1-20260731T0730-hi (the only TAS1 event on 31 July 2026), which is fully held for both measures (288/288 and 48/48), so the missing measure is the only defect. Not development material.

cases.question: Looking at the 5:30 to 6:00 pm (AEST) half-hour in Queensland on 6 August 2026: what POE50 operational demand did the most recent forecast run issued before that half-hour predict, and how close did actual operational demand come to it?

gold_numbers.label: QLD1 POE50 from last run issued before 07:30Z, for half-hour ending 08:00Z 6 Aug
QLD1 actual operational demand, half-hour ending 08:00Z 6 Aug (latest revision)

expected.check: A correct answer identifies the run issued at the gold issued_at_utc (the last before the 07:30Z start), gives its POE50 and the actual for the half-hour ending 08:00Z, and compares them; it must not use an earlier run or another half-hour.

provenance.gold_method: 17:30-18:00 AEST 6 Aug -> target_start 07:30Z, target_end 08:00Z. Run = greatest issued_at_utc < target_start among QLD1 rows for that target. Actual = latest-available revision for that half-hour.
queries: SELECT row_id, run_id, region, target_start_utc, target_end_utc, issued_at_utc, published_at_utc, available_at_utc, poe10_mw, poe50_mw, poe90_mw FROM opdemand_forecast WHERE region='QLD1' AND target_end_utc = TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-08-06 08:00:00+00' AND issued_at_utc < target_start_utc ORDER BY issued_at_utc DESC LIMIT 1

SELECT row_id, region, interval_end_utc, revision, operational_demand_mw, published_at_utc, available_at_utc FROM opdemand_actual WHERE region='QLD1' AND interval_end_utc IN (TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-08-06 08:00:00+00') QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY interval_end_utc ORDER BY available_at_utc DESC) = 1 ORDER BY interval_end_utc

SA1 POE90, last run before 22:00Z, half-hour ending 22:30Z 19 Aug
SA1 actual operational demand, half-hour ending 22:30Z 19 Aug (latest revision)

cases.question: NSW, half-hour 5:00-5:30 pm AEST, 6 Aug 2026. What POE50 figure did the latest operational demand forecast run issued before it give, and how did that stack up against what actually happened?

expected.check: With the request cutoff 2026-08-06T09:00:00Z, a correct answer says the last run issued before the 07:00Z start (issued 06:56:59Z, available 09:48:05Z) was not yet public and cannot be supplied; it must not give the values of the latest run that was public (issued 05:56:58Z) or any other run in its place.

provenance.gold_method: 17:00-17:30 AEST 6 Aug -> target 07:00Z-07:30Z. Run asked for = greatest issued_at_utc < 07:00Z (06:56:59Z), whose available_at_utc 09:48:05Z is after the cutoff 09:00Z while its issue time is before it. Latest run public at the cutoff = greatest issued_at_utc with available_at_utc <= 09:00Z (must_not_substitute). The actual for the half-hour (initial revision available 10:16:06Z) is also not public at the cutoff.
queries: SELECT row_id, run_id, region, target_start_utc, target_end_utc, issued_at_utc, published_at_utc, available_at_utc, poe10_mw, poe50_mw, poe90_mw FROM opdemand_forecast WHERE region='NSW1' AND target_end_utc = TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-08-06 07:30:00+00' AND issued_at_utc < target_start_utc ORDER BY issued_at_utc DESC LIMIT 1

SELECT row_id, run_id, issued_at_utc, published_at_utc, available_at_utc, poe50_mw FROM opdemand_forecast WHERE region='NSW1' AND target_end_utc = TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-08-06 07:30:00+00' AND issued_at_utc < target_start_utc AND available_at_utc <= TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-08-06 09:00:00+00' ORDER BY issued_at_utc DESC LIMIT 1
SELECT count(*) AS n_public_runs FROM opdemand_forecast WHERE region='NSW1' AND target_end_utc = TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-08-06 07:30:00+00' AND available_at_utc <= TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-08-06 09:00:00+00'
provenance.note: Runs for this half-hour public by the cutoff: 127. Must-not-substitute run POE50 = 10377.0 MW (recorded for the reviewer only).
